title: A multistage cp.async pipeline
brief: Take a tensor-core GEMM (bfloat16 in, float32 accumulate) whose block loads and computes in turn, and give it a 2 to 4 stage cp.async pipeline. Report TFLOP/s and the speedup over one stage.
hints: The first run compiles the CUDA source with nvcc, which takes 30 to 90 seconds because the kernel is instantiated for five stage counts. Later runs reuse the build.
Start with the Python half: stage_smem_bytes, max_stages, and schedule need no GPU. The tests check schedule against a model ring buffer before they touch the kernel.
At the top of loop iteration kt, groups 0 to kt + STAGES - 2 are committed, and tile kt is group kt. How many groups may still be pending for tile kt to be safe?
The slot you load into at iteration kt is the one that held tile kt - 1. Why is it safe to overwrite after the __syncthreads, and unsafe before?
Commit a group on every iteration, even when there is no tile left to load. Every thread's wait_group count then means the same thing.
